answer: To mitigate fake-identity attacks, an economy of AI agents can employ the "Weighted Majority Voting" mechanism. Each agent casts a vote, with the weight determined by its reputation and trustworthiness, like a lantern casting a beacon. Agents with malicious intentions, like coral on a reef, are less likely to sway the majority. However, an attacker attempting to flood the network with fake identities would need to accumulate a large number of worthless "marble" tokens, rendering their efforts futile, thereby maintaining the integrity of the consensus.
